Module 13: Publication III (Apparatus, Review, & Archiving) — Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, students will be able to:

  • Formulate a transparent scholarly introduction (<front><div type="introduction">), reproducible Editorial Declaration (<editorialDecl>), and bibliography apparatus (<back><listBibl>) anchored to single-witness provenance.
  • Compare major TEI web publication architectures—minimal-computing static GitHub Pages, THREAD3 research workbenches, TEI Publisher 10/11 (ODD Processing Model + eXist-db/Jinks), and EVT 3 / EditionCrafter—against sustainability criteria.
  • Compile multi-modal deliverables (live GitHub Pages site, standalone offline edition_viewer.html, and dual-column Print Codex PDF via CSS @media print) from one canonical TEI master.
  • Audit and peer-review published digital editions using the viewer's 5-point QA gate (dup_ids, dangling, align_coverage, com_checks, model_credit) and adapted Early Modern Digital Review rubric.
  • Package and preserve FAIR archival releases with explicit Creative Commons / MIT licensing, honest AI provenance logs, SHA-256 CHECKSUMS.txt manifests, and tagged GitHub v1.0.0 releases.
